title: A vibrating string three ways: CPU vertices, TSL, morph targets
question: To animate a plucked string, is it cheaper to rewrite its vertices on the CPU, displace them in a TSL vertex shader (lesson 13's choice), or blend a morph target, for the 6 strings of one guitar and for 600 strings?
hypothesis: With 6 strings the three are indistinguishable; with 600, rewriting vertices costs CPU time proportional to the vertex count and an upload every frame, while TSL and morph targets cost almost nothing on the CPU.

predictions.metric: median CPU ms per frame, 6 strings
predictions.predicted: the three within 0.3 ms of each other

predictions.metric: median CPU ms per frame, 600 strings
predictions.predicted: cpu at least 5x tsl; morph within 2x tsl

predictions.metric: median GPU ms per frame, 600 strings
predictions.predicted: the three within 30% of each other
